capture.final_message:
Treat all four quantified statements as independently true; then each displayed `Iff` follows by proving both sides without using the opposite hypothesis.

The common mechanism is that `chromaticNumber G` is the least number of colors:

- Transport a coloring along a graph isomorphism (and its inverse) to establish invariance of `Colorable`.
- Use the threshold characterization
  \[
  G\text{ is }n\text{-colorable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \chi(G)\le n.
  \]
  Then \(\chi(G)=n+1\) is exactly “\(G\) is \((n+1)\)-colorable but not \(n\)-colorable.”
- Show \(n\le\chi(G)\) iff every coloring \(G\to\mathrm{Fin}(n)\) is surjective. A non-surjective coloring can be compressed to fewer than \(n\) colors; conversely, if \(\chi(G)<n\), embed a coloring using fewer colors into `Fin n`, producing a non-surjective coloring.
- Given an \(n\)-coloring and a pairwise-adjacent family \(f:\iota\to V\), the composite of \(f\) with the coloring is injective: adjacent vertices receive distinct colors. Thus \(\iota\) injects into `Fin n`, yielding `Nat.card ι ≤ n`.

Finally assemble the outer conjunction and the two equivalences by invoking these standalone facts in both directions.
